Q: Is it possible to switch from dark mode to light mode after installing breeze in dark mode? A:

For me, the issue was fixed by removing all classes with dark: I believe that overrides the setup on app.css

example before (only dark mode worked)

class="bg-zinc-50 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-900"

By removing these classes, the light mode worked.

Q: Tailwind won't show light mode and only shows dark mode styles A:

For me the issue fix was to remove all classes with dark: I believe that overrides the setup on app.css

example before (only dark mode worked)

class="bg-zinc-50 dark:border-zinc-700 dark:bg-zinc-900"

After removing these classes light mode worked.

Q: How Can i solve this "Try signing in with a different account." problem with Next-Auth? A:

Just redirect to the root domain without subdomain: www: eg:: www.example.com to example.com

Q: 1 same object that can be one of multiple classes instance. C++ equivalente for a Python code with language-agnostic code style A:

easy to remember in the scenario about a programmer that works with multiple languages, with the preference for "language-agnostic code style"

C++ is not Python, and Python is not C++. Honestly, trying to shoehorn C++ into looking like Python or vice-versa is not worth the effort. If the "dots" and "arrows" in C++, basic fundamentals, will confuse the programmer, then frankly the programmer either needs to learn C++ properly, or use another language.

Line-by-line or similar types of code translations from language A to language B is not a good idea. You will get to the "all your base are belong to us" scenario for language B.

The proper way to translate from language A to language B is to

  1. Know both language A and language B to the appropriate level of competence.
  2. Know what language A is attempting to accomplish at a high level
  3. Throw language A's implementation away, but remembering what was being accomplished.
  4. Implement the solution in language B using language B's idioms and best practices.
